newsitem.title: JAPAN: British Airways to increase London-Japan flights.
newsitem.headline: British Airways to increase London-Japan flights.

text.p: British Airways Plc (BA) said on Tuesday it will increase the number of flights between London and two Japanese airports from March 30.

Chief executive Robert Ayling told a news conference in Tokyo that the company will operate daily flights or seven flights a week between Heathrow and the Kansai International Airport near Osaka, up from five flights per week.
It will also increase its flights between Heathrow and Nagoya in central Japan to three per week from two, Ayling said.
"If it wasn't for the lack of slots, we could offer more flights," said Ayling.

British Airways has also recently started basing cabin crews in the Kansai region. Fifty crew members are now based in the region, which includes the cities of Osaka, Kyoto, Nara and Kobe, the company said in statement.
On a proposed tie-up with AMR Corp's American Airlines, Ayling said that an alliance would allow British Airways to operate a global network.
